summary.oneLiner: L.G. Balakrishnan & Bros Limited (LGB), established in 1956, is a leading Indian manufacturer of transmission chains, sprockets and metal-formed components for automotive and industrial applications, marketed under its 'ROLON' brand.
summary.business: LGB manufactures chains, sprockets and metal-formed parts for automotive applications across two business segments: Transmission (chains, sprockets, tensioners, belts) and Metal Forming (fine blanking for precision sheet metal parts, machined components and wire drawing products, used internally as well as sold to other chain manufacturers and spring steel manufacturers). The Company serves a diversified base of Indian and global OEMs as well as the automotive aftermarket.

currentContext.strengths: Long-standing brand 'ROLON' with a reputation as a trusted leader in high-performance engineered components for the automotive industry, built since incorporation in 1956|Diversified customer base spanning Indian and global OEMs plus the aftermarket, with exports to about 30 countries limiting reliance on any single market|Vertically integrated metal forming / fine blanking and wire-drawing capability that supplies both its own chain manufacturing and external sales to other chain manufacturers and spring steel manufacturers
currentContext.strategies: Focus on being responsive to new opportunities while retaining existing clientele and markets, managing the cost base, and driving operational excellence to protect corporate value amid global economic and geopolitical uncertainty.|HR strategy centred on skill development, career growth and structured career-pathing to retain and develop employee talent.|The Board maintains a stated track record of consistent dividend payout and dividend growth, backed by consistently growing revenues and earnings, governed by a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy published on the Company's website. Profits are also reinvested via transfers to the General Reserve, with the balance retained in the Surplus in the Profit and Loss Account, rather than distributed.
currentContext.expansion: During FY2025-26, the Company added to its renewable/self-generation power capacity, having installed and commissioned a 7.12 MW windmill and a 15.25 MWp DC rooftop/ground-mounted solar plant during the year. It is now developing a further rooftop solar project (2.6 MWp DC capacity) and a Group Captive Power project (12.5 MWp DC capacity), both targeted for commissioning in FY2026-27.
currentContext.mdna: India's economic trajectory is expected to remain promising, supported by the Government's continuing push through Make in India initiatives, stable rural demand from rising household consumption, and strategic reforms.|The India-EU free trade agreement has been finalised, which management expects to further strengthen economic activity and support future growth.|The Indian economy was resilient during the year, supported by Government policies, short-term GST rate cuts, and the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, seen as key enablers for boosting the country's manufacturing capabilities.|Near-term threats flagged include uncertainty in the global economic environment, fluctuations in raw material prices, and an evolving geopolitical landscape including trade and tariff wars, which may cause instability and volatile consumption in end markets.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
